# Bitcoin / A network in time

An interactive visualization of 150 curated dates and 22,374 blocks from genesis through 2026-10-19 UTC. Atom and Classic are two layouts of identical measurements. Event selection is editorial; coincidence does not establish causation.

Seven signals: blocks = number of teeth; non-coinbase transactions = ring 1; individual block weight = tooth length; total block fees in BTC = ring 2; arithmetic mean block difficulty = ring 3; estimated hashrate in EH/s = ring 4; active addresses = dots. Transactions, fees and hashrate use shared release maxima; difficulty uses log10(mean)/log10(release maximum). Tooth length is 0.12 + 1.35*weight/4,000,000; width is fixed. Addresses per dot: 1,000 detail / 8,000 grid, rounded down, caps 1,500 / 180. Addresses are not people.

Block-header UTC days differ from CoinMetrics normalized Median-Time-Past days. Blockchain.com and mempool.space block hashes/timestamps are matched, with Blockstream boundary checks. Per-block fees come from mempool.space. CoinMetrics supplies HashRate and AdrActCnt. BigQuery has not run. Mempool, transfer estimates, fee distributions and unsupported scores are not shown. Missing data remains null; missing and zero have no arc, with distinct numeric labels. Lighting, positions and animation are decorative.

/data/snapshots.json contains schema-2 daily records. /data/blocks.json contains [height,sizeBytes,weightWU,txCountIncludingCoinbase]. /data/block-details/YYYY-MM-DD.json contains full block records used by the hover/tap inspector. /data/provenance.json records source metadata, scales and limitations. Event sources are attached to each snapshot. Original source: https://github.com/vyalya/bitcoin-data-driven-geometry
